LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal: For a pair (X,Y) with joint law p, the first marginal is the probability distribution of X obtained by retaining the first coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal: For a pair (X,Y) with joint law p, the second marginal is the probability distribution of Y obtained by retaining the second coordinate.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map: If a map f sends an outcome to a pair (X,Y), then the first marginal of the law of f equals the law obtained by sending the outcome directly to X.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map: If a map f sends an outcome to a pair (X,Y), then the second marginal of the law of f equals the law obtained by sending the outcome directly to Y.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map_p: Draw a source outcome ω from a probability mass function p. The first marginal of the joint law of (X(ω),Y(ω)) is the law of X(ω) under p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map_p: Draw a source outcome ω from a probability mass function p. The second marginal of the joint law of (X(ω),Y(ω)) is the law of Y(ω) under p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map_s: The first marginal of the swapped pair (Y,X) is the second marginal of the original pair (X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map_s: The second marginal of the swapped pair (Y,X) is the first marginal of the original pair (X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_apply: For a joint law p with a finite second alphabet, the first marginal assigns mass p_X(a) = ∑(b) p(a,b) to a.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_apply: For a joint law p with a finite first alphabet, the second marginal assigns mass p_Y(b) = ∑ₐ p(a,b) to b.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal: For a triple (X,Y,Z) with law p, this is the joint distribution of (X,Y) obtained by discarding Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal_ma: If f maps outcomes to triples, the first–second marginal of the law of f is the distribution of the pair of its first two coordinates.
The first–second marginal of the law of (X,Y,Z) equals the joint law of (X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal: For a triple (X,Y,Z) with law p, this is the joint distribution of (X,Z) obtained by discarding Y.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal: For a triple (X,Y,Z) with law p, this is the joint distribution of (Y,Z) obtained by discarding X.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal: For a triple (X,Y,Z) with law p, this is the probability distribution of its third coordinate Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_: If f maps outcomes to triples, the first–third marginal of its law is the distribution obtained by mapping each outcome to the first and third coordinates of f.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal_: If f maps outcomes to triples, the second–third marginal of its law is the distribution obtained by mapping each outcome to the second and third coordinates of f.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_map: If f maps outcomes to triples, the third marginal of its law is the distribution obtained by mapping each outcome to the third coordinate of f.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_: The first–third marginal of the law of (X,Y,Z) equals the joint law of (X,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal_: The second–third marginal of the law of (X,Y,Z) equals the joint law of (Y,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_map: The third marginal of the law of (X,Y,Z) equals the law of Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_: The first–third marginal after swapping X and Y has the original joint law of (Y,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal_: The second–third marginal after swapping X and Y has the original joint law of (X,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_map: Swapping X and Y in a triple (X,Y,Z) preserves the law of its third coordinate Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_: For a triple law p with a finite second alphabet, the mass of (a,c) in the first–third marginal is ∑(b) p(a,b,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal_: For a triple law p with a finite first alphabet, the mass of (b,c) in the second–third marginal is ∑ₐ p(a,b,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_app: For a triple law p with finite first and second alphabets, the mass of c in the third marginal is ∑ₐ ∑(b) p(a,b,c).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_fstMargi: The probability of the joint outcome (a,b) is at most the mass of the first marginal at a. This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_sndMargi: The probability of the joint outcome (a,b) is at most the mass of the second marginal at b. This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_fstThird: The probability of the joint outcome (a,b,c) is at most the mass of the first–third marginal at (a,c). This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_sndThird: The probability of the joint outcome (a,b,c) is at most the mass of the second–third marginal at (b,c). This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_thirdMar: The probability of the joint outcome (a,b,c) is at most the mass of the third marginal at c. This statement assumes the first and second alphabets are finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_eq_zero_of_: If the mass of the first marginal at a is zero, the joint outcome (a,b) also has probability zero. This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
If the mass of the second marginal at b is zero, the joint outcome (a,b) also has probability zero. This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_ne_ze: If the joint outcome (a,b) has positive probability, the mass of the first marginal at a is positive. This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_ne_ze: If the joint outcome (a,b) has positive probability, the mass of the second marginal at b is positive. This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_eq_zero_of_: If the mass of the first–third marginal at (a,c) is zero, the joint outcome (a,b,c) also has probability zero. This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
If the mass of the second–third marginal at (b,c) is zero, the joint outcome (a,b,c) also has probability zero. This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
If the mass of the third marginal at c is zero, the joint outcome (a,b,c) also has probability zero. This statement assumes the first and second alphabets are finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_: If the joint outcome (a,b,c) has positive probability, the mass of the first–third marginal at (a,c) is positive. This statement assumes the second alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal_: If the joint outcome (a,b,c) has positive probability, the mass of the second–third marginal at (b,c) is positive. This statement assumes the first alphabet is finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_ne_: If the joint outcome (a,b,c) has positive probability, the mass of the third marginal at c is positive. This statement assumes the first and second alphabets are finite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy: For the coordinates of a finite joint distribution p, the conditional entropy of X given Y is defined in nats by H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) − H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo: For the coordinates of a finite joint distribution p, the mutual information between X and Y is defined in nats by I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) − H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo: For the coordinates of a finite joint distribution p, the conditional mutual information between X and Y given Z is defined in nats by I(X;Y|Z) = H(X,Z) + H(Y,Z) − H(Z) − H(X,Y,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf: Let X and Y have finite alphabets. Their joint law is the pushforward of the source probability mass function p by (X,Y). Under this law, the conditional entropy of X given Y is H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) − H(Y), in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf: Let X and Y have finite alphabets. Their joint law is the pushforward of the source probability mass function p by (X,Y). Under this law, the mutual information between X and Y is I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) − H(X,Y), in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf: Let X, Y and Z have finite alphabets. Their joint law is the pushforward of the source probability mass function p by (X,Y,Z). Under this law, the conditional mutual information is I(X;Y|Z) = H(X,Z) + H(Y,Z) − H(Z) − H(X,Y,Z), in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_sw: For a finite pair law, swapping its coordinates preserves mutual information, I(Y;X) = I(X;Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_swap: For finite-valued variables on a common source, I(Y;X) = I(X;Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_ma: In a finite triple law, swapping the first two coordinates gives I(Y;X|Z) = I(X;Y|Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued variables on a common source, I(Y;X|Z) = I(X;Y|Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_fst: Under a joint probability mass function p, the entropy of the first coordinate equals the entropy of the first marginal of p. Only the first coordinate needs a finite alphabet.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_snd: Under a joint probability mass function p, the entropy of the second coordinate equals the entropy of the second marginal of p. Only the second coordinate needs a finite alphabet.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_fs: For a finite pair law p, the joint entropy of the two coordinate projections equals the entropy of p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fst: For a finite pair law p, the conditional entropy of its first coordinate given its second equals the conditional entropy computed directly from p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_fst_: For a finite pair law p, the mutual information of the two coordinate projections equals the mutual information computed directly from p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_third: Under a joint probability mass function p on triples, the entropy of the third coordinate equals the entropy of the third marginal of p. Only the third coordinate needs a finite alphabet.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_fs: Under a joint probability mass function p on triples, the joint entropy of the first and third coordinates equals the entropy of their marginal law. Only the first and third coordinates need finite alphabets.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_sn: Under a joint probability mass function p on triples, the joint entropy of the second and third coordinates equals the entropy of their marginal law. Only the second and third coordinates need finite alphabets.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For a finite triple law p, I(X;Y|Z) of the three coordinate projections equals the conditional mutual information computed directly from p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq: For the coordinates of a finite joint law p, the conditional entropy of X given Y satisfies H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) − H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq: For the coordinates of a finite joint law p, the mutual information between X and Y satisfies I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) − H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For the coordinates of a finite joint law p, the conditional mutual information between X and Y given Z satisfies I(X;Y|Z) = H(X,Z) + H(Y,Z) − H(Z) − H(X,Y,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_entrop: For the coordinates of a finite pair law, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(Y) + H(X|Y).
For the coordinates of a finite pair law, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_eq: For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(Y) + H(X|Y).
For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_chain_rul: For the coordinates of a finite pair law, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(Y) + H(X|Y).
For the coordinates of a finite pair law, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_ch: For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(Y) + H(X|Y).
For finite-valued random variables X and Y, the entropy chain rule gives H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq: For X and Y with finite alphabets on a common source, the increase in joint entropy when X is added to Y is H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) − H(Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For X, Y and Z with finite alphabets on a common source, interchanging the order of X and Y preserves their joint entropy conditional on Z, so H(Y,X|Z) = H(X,Y|Z).
For finite-valued variables, H(X,Y|Z) = H(Y|Z) + H(X|Y,Z).
For finite-valued variables, H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z) + H(Y|X,Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq: For finite-valued X and Y, I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) − H(X,Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued X, Y and Z, I(X;Y|Z) = H(X,Z) + H(Y,Z) − H(Z) − H(X,Y,Z).
For X, Y and Z with finite alphabets on a common source, the information Y supplies about X given Z is I(X;Y|Z) = H(X|Z) − H(X|Y,Z).
For X, Y and Z with finite alphabets on a common source, the information X supplies about Y given Z is I(X;Y|Z) = H(Y|Z) − H(Y|X,Z).
For finite-valued X, Y and Z, I(X;Y|Z) = H(X|Z) + H(Y|Z) − H(X,Y|Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq_ent: For coordinates X,Y of a finite pair law, I(X;Y) = H(X) − H(X|Y).
For coordinates X,Y of a finite pair law, I(X;Y) = H(Y) − H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq_e: For finite-valued X and Y on a common source, I(X;Y) = H(X) − H(X|Y).
For finite-valued X and Y on a common source, I(X;Y) = H(Y) − H(Y|X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_cond: For three finite-valued variables, I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X) − I(X;Z|Y) − H(Y|X,Z) + I(X;Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_map_di: If X has finite law p, the mutual information of the diagonal pair (X,X) equals H(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_self: Every finite-valued random variable X satisfies I(X;X) = H(X).
